p.SCOPE: This document defines how one owner-facing central session derives a stable, resumable campaign goal from the authoritative user-local `plan.toml`. The output is local `GOAL.md`: useful to a harness goal field, a resumed session and a human, but never a second plan and never project authority. The same snapshot emits local `GOAL-CLAUDE.txt`, the exact bounded slash command a human can paste into Claude Code.

facts.GOAL-IS-LOCAL: The outputs live at `~/.vibe/steward/contexts/<context-id>/{GOAL.md,GOAL-CLAUDE.txt}`. They are never committed, mirrored, packaged, or used to grant another contributor authority.
facts.GOAL-HAS-NO-LLM: Canonical bytes use no model completion, paraphrase, chat history or provider call. An LLM may explain the result separately; it never rewrites `GOAL.md`.

p.GOAL-NODE-SETTING: Context `settings.toml` may name `goal_node = "<stable-node-id>"`. The id must exist, have kind `campaign` or `portfolio`, and not be `accepted`, `dropped`, or `superseded`. An explicit owner selection always wins.

p.UNIQUE-INFERENCE: With no setting, infer only when exactly one non-terminal top-level `campaign` exists (a campaign with no campaign ancestor). Zero or several candidates is `GOAL_NODE_AMBIGUOUS` and produces no write. Never choose by recency, declaration order, current UI row, model preference or title similarity.

p.SELECTED-SUBTREE: The selected node plus every transitive child by `parent` is the goal subtree. Dependencies may point outside it and remain visible as external prerequisites; they do not silently expand goal ownership.

facts.SNAPSHOT-READ: Read `settings.toml`, `custody.toml` and raw `plan.toml` bytes once. Parse and render from those exact bytes. `plan_sha256` is lowercase SHA-256 of the raw plan bytes.
facts.SNAPSHOT-AUTH: Before rendering, require `custody.state = "held"` and exact current session/holder identity. Workers, non-holders, `vacant`, and `offering` may diagnose staleness but cannot write.
facts.SNAPSHOT-RECHECK: Render both outputs to same-directory temporary files, then re-read the plan hash, selected setting, profile and custody epoch/holder before publication. Rename the Claude command first and `GOAL.md` last; the latter's marker certifies the former's hash. On drift, discard and take at most one fresh snapshot; a second drift refuses as `GOAL_INPUT_MOVED`.

p.ORDER: Hierarchy order is deterministic pre-order. Children sort by numeric `order`, then stable `id`; mandate rows keep their declaration order. No map/hash iteration order enters output.

facts.PROJECT-OUTCOME: **Outcome:** selected node id and title, followed by its own acceptance lines. Text is copied verbatim, never summarized.
facts.PROJECT-MANDATES: **Governing mandates:** ordered union of mandate ids referenced by non-dropped/non-superseded nodes in the subtree. Render id, disposition and exact text; accepted mandates remain visible as laws already established.
facts.PROJECT-BOUNDARY: **Accepted boundary:** every accepted node whose parent is outside the subtree or is not accepted. This is the maximal accepted frontier: it compresses accepted descendants without losing where non-terminal work begins.
facts.PROJECT-CANDIDATES: **Current candidates:** every `candidate` node in pre-order, including its acceptance lines. A candidate is never described as complete merely because bytes exist.
facts.PROJECT-ROUTE: **Remaining route:** every subtree node not in `accepted | dropped | superseded | deferred`, in pre-order, with id, title, state and explicit dependencies. Ancestors remain, so a short UI frontier cannot erase distant stages.
facts.PROJECT-DEFERRED: **Deferred horizon:** deferred subtree nodes, with their acceptance/revisit condition. Dropped and superseded nodes are omitted from execution but their mandate dispositions remain visible above.
facts.PROJECT-CLOSURE: **Completion proof:** the selected node's acceptance plus acceptance lines of every non-accepted descendant whose kind is `gate`, in pre-order. Empty queues and completed UI rows are explicitly insufficient.
facts.PROJECT-PROFILE: **Execution profile:** one fixed paragraph for canonical `ultra` or `standard`, copied from this protocol. Both name the identical quality floor; only atom/checkpoint cadence differs.
facts.PROJECT-CONTINUITY: **Continuation law:** fixed text requires complete plan re-read after compact/resume, regeneration on stale inputs, continued execution across intermediate atoms, and stopping only for an owner-only decision, external blocker, or central handoff.

bytes.title: 5. Canonical bytes and marker

p.MARKER: The first line is exactly one HTML comment with fields in this order:

bytes.fence: <!-- steward-goal schema=1 plan_id="example" plan_revision=7 goal_node="BUILD" planning_profile="ultra" plan_sha256="0123...cdef" claude_condition_sha256="fedc...3210" -->

p.BYTE-LAW: UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, one trailing newline, exact heading order from §4, no timestamp, absolute path, session id, holder id, harness, model, token count or chat text. Markdown bullet text is copied from TOML without stylistic rewriting. Identical plan bytes + selected node + canonical profile produce byte-identical `GOAL.md`.

p.PROFILE-TEXT: Canonical profile paragraph: `ultra` — “Use extended reasoning across the full route; larger coherent atoms are allowed only while review and evidence remain bounded. The completeness, review and gate floor is unchanged.” `standard` — “Use smaller atoms, explicit per-claim evidence and a backscan after every completed parent. The completeness, review and gate floor is unchanged.”

p.CONTINUITY-TEXT: Canonical continuation paragraph: “After compact or resume, re-read the complete plan and refresh this goal if stale. Continue across accepted intermediate atoms; a short UI plan, context loss, difficulty, or worker termination is not completion. Stop only for an owner-only decision, an external blocker, or a central custody handoff. Declare completion only when every completion proof below is satisfied.”

p.CLAUDE-OBSERVED-SURFACE: Claude Code 2.1.220 exposes `/goal <condition>` and rejects a condition longer than 4000 JavaScript string units. Adapter epoch 1 therefore caps the condition at **4000 UTF-16 code units**. This observed client limit belongs only to the adapter; it does not constrain canonical `GOAL.md`.

p.CLAUDE-FILE: `GOAL-CLAUDE.txt` is one logical line plus one LF: exact ASCII prefix `/goal ` followed by the condition. The condition contains no newline; every input whitespace run is collapsed to one ASCII space. A human copies the whole trimmed file and pastes it into the interactive prompt. Agents never invoke slash commands on the user's behalf.

p.CLAUDE-CONDITION: The condition is assembled in this fixed order: (1) “Complete campaign [id] title exactly as stewardship plan.toml revision N defines, including every non-terminal descendant and all completion proof in GOAL.md.”; (2) candidate ids/titles; (3) non-terminal direct child route ids/titles/states; (4) “After compact/resume re-read plan.toml and GOAL.md; do not stop at a short UI plan, an intermediate atom, difficulty or a worker/process ending; stop only for an owner-only decision, external blocker or central handoff; the goal is met only when the selected node is accepted with all required descendants/gates and owner inspection.”

p.CLAUDE-BOUNDING: Bounding never truncates the mandatory first/fourth clauses. Add candidate entries in pre-order, then direct-child route entries in order. If the next full `id + title + state` entry would exceed 4000 units, retry that section with ids only. If ids still exceed, keep the longest prefix that fits and append `+N more in GOAL.md`. The count is exact. If mandatory clauses alone exceed the cap, keep `GOAL.md` but refuse the adapter as `GOAL_CLAUDE_BASE_TOO_LONG`; never cut arbitrary characters.

p.CLAUDE-HASH: `claude_condition_sha256` is lowercase SHA-256 of UTF-8 condition bytes without `/goal ` or trailing LF. A current GOAL marker and `GOAL-CLAUDE.txt` must agree on this hash. On `GOAL_CLAUDE_BASE_TOO_LONG`, the marker carries literal `unavailable` and no command file exists; canonical GOAL remains current while the adapter refusal is reported.

p.STALE-TEST: A goal is current only when its marker schema, plan id, plan revision, goal node, canonical profile and raw plan SHA equal current inputs, and either the actual Claude condition hash matches or the current deterministic render repeats the marker's `unavailable` refusal. Missing/malformed required output is stale. A changed interaction mode alone is not stale because it changes narration, not goal semantics.

p.REFRESH-TRIGGERS: Check at central-session start, after compaction/resume, after every accepted plan mutation, and after owner changes `goal_node` or planning profile. The current holder refreshes before further campaign execution; non-holders report only.

facts.REFUSE-AMBIGUOUS: `GOAL_NODE_AMBIGUOUS`: zero/multiple inferable campaigns and no valid explicit selection.
facts.REFUSE-INVALID: `GOAL_NODE_INVALID`: absent, wrong kind, or already terminal selected id.
facts.REFUSE-PLAN: `GOAL_PLAN_INVALID`: duplicate ids, missing parent/dependency/mandate, cycle, invalid current node or unknown state/kind needed by the projection.
facts.REFUSE-MOVED: `GOAL_INPUT_MOVED`: second snapshot drift; no output replacement.
facts.REFUSE-CLAUDE-LIMIT: `GOAL_CLAUDE_BASE_TOO_LONG`: mandatory condition clauses alone exceed the observed client cap; canonical GOAL remains available.

p.SKILL-NOW-COMPANION-LATER: v0.2 ships the `steward-goal` agent skill as the executable procedure. A future separate `vibe-steward goal render` companion may implement these exact bytes and refusals. It is never a `vibe.exe` subcommand, and adding it cannot change this format without a new schema/version.
